The function $y=f(x)$ above is continuous on the interval $[-3,4]$ and differentiable on $(-3,4).$ Complete the sentence below.

*The mean value theorem states that there exists a point $c\in (-3,4)$ such that $\text{_______}\,.$ *
feedback.worked_solution:
Given that $f(x)$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on  $(a,b)$, the mean value theorem states the following:

*There exists a point $c\in (a,b)$ such that*

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

In our case, we have $a=-3$ and $b=4.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(4)-f(-3)}{4-(-3)} \\  & =\frac{1-(-3)}{4+3} \\  & =\frac{4}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the complete sentence is as follows:

*The mean value theorem states that there exists a point $c\in (-3,4)$ such that ${f}^{′}(c)=\frac{4}{7}.$*
